summary: Shipped the per-guest limit of PveBackupFreshnessLow (PR 624, ws-20261029-pve-backup-weekly-freshness) to the monitoring VM's Prometheus by installing config/prometheus/rules/pve-host-incident.yml from main a39eade5e at 2026-10-30T00:48:07Z (02:48 local). The alert holds a guest whose published proxmox_backup_max_age_seconds is over 48 hours (CT 108, weekly job ct108-nightly, 8.5 days) to that limit and every other guest to 30 hours, so CT 108 no longer pages for about 5.75 days of every week. A targeted Ansible play that uses the monitoring_vm role's own copy parameters (root:prometheus, 0640), validated by promtool before it replaced the live file, followed by a SIGHUP reload without a restart; only that file and one backup copy changed in /etc/prometheus/rules. The firing alert for guest 108 (critical since about 09:30Z on 2026-10-29) cleared at the first evaluation after the reload.

Both held.

The 22-file replay of the role's rule copies made on 2026-10-26 was not repeated.

No separate stdin run was made this time.

SIGHUP via systemctl kill --kill-whom=main at 00:48:14Z; journal 'Completed loading of configuration file' at 00:48:15Z, totalDuration 177 ms; prometheus_config_last_reload_successful=1; the service was not restarted (main process 685 throughout). A second reload at 00:54:19Z (117 ms, also successful) followed a change of a different rule file, fleet-woodpecker-agent-records.yml, modified at 00:54 by someone else; it is not part of this apply.

verification.check: Alert loaded with the new expression and cleared
verification.observed: The play's read-back from the running Prometheus (rules API): PveBackupFreshnessLow, group pve_host_incident (15 s interval), query carries proxmox_backup_max_age_seconds, lastError none. The alert instance for guest 108 that had been firing was gone at the first evaluation (last evaluation 00:48:29Z): health ok, state inactive, 0 alerts, no ALERTS series; the alerts firing on the 0mcp Prometheus went from 17 to 16, the only difference being PveBackupFreshnessLow for guest 108, and none appeared.

At about 00:50Z the limits the rule computes per guest were 108000 s (30 h) for guests 101, 104, 107 and 109 and 734400 s (8.5 days) for guest 108; the ages of the last success were 70,994 s (101, 104), 76,664 s (107, 109) and 166,116 s (108): no guest over its limit. The old fixed 30 h rule read true for guest 108 only. The collector (fleet-state PR 619, installed 2026-10-28) already published proxmox_backup_max_age_seconds for all five guests.

Not run this time. On 2026-10-26 (receipt 2026-10-26-pve-host-daily-low-alert-monitoring-live-apply) make live-apply-service service=grafana env=production stopped at the vulnerability budget gate (host scan for monitoring older than its 7-day limit) and at the immutable guest replacement gate (needs ALLOW_IN_PLACE_MUTATION=true) and would trigger a restic backup afterwards, and make converge-monitoring runs seven playbooks; the same targeted one-file play with the monitoring_vm role's own copy parameters was used again. Those gates were not re-tested today.

notes: The rule was merged in PR 624 (squash commit a39eade5eeef483f954ffb8cf019d706040586c0); this receipt records shipping it. The collector side is baditaflorin/fleet-state PR 619 (hypervisor-0docker/libexec/pve-host-health-metrics.py, installed on the hypervisor on 2026-10-28), which publishes proxmox_backup_max_age_seconds and looks back 10 days for a weekly guest. The same targeted approach is recorded in 2026-10-26-pve-host-daily-low-alert-monitoring-live-apply and 2026-10-12-scanopy-retag-discover-monitoring-live-apply.

Rollback: copy /etc/prometheus/rules/pve-host-incident.yml.pre-weekly-vzdump-20261030T004755Z over pve-host-incident.yml and send SIGHUP to 0mcp-prometheus.service (systemctl kill --kill-whom=main --signal=HUP 0mcp-prometheus.service); the alert for guest 108 then fires again 30 hours after each Sunday 03:30 run until its next run.
